title: Two conjectures of Wormald on Hamilton cycles in tournaments

authors.name: Deep Bhattacharjee
authors.affiliation: Formerly, Electro-Gravitational Space Propulsion Laboratory (EGSPL), Bhubaneswar, Odisha 751030, India

journal_fit: The exact tournament invariant, cyclic formulas and algebraic proof fit the journal's combinatorial and algebraic scope. The newer global Hamilton-cycle asymptotic of Divoux and Wang is explicitly credited; the manuscript does not claim that broader theorem as its contribution.
contribution: The manuscript proves Wormald's Conjectures 2 and 6: a determinant formula for every regular tournament gives the rational-square property, and an exact cyclic formula gives the limit cosh(1)/cos(1). This revision details the analytic Hessian identification, proves quantitative positive-definiteness and supplies a direct spectral-radius argument.

formalization_scope: The unchanged Lean proof tree has a complete successful build and 23 axiom reports using only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. It formalizes the determinant algebra and cyclic limit after identifying H with det(E^T F E). The analytic identification, asymptotic expansion, spectral bounds and new quantitative corollary have written proofs and are not claimed as Lean-formalized. Fresh exact checks verify 41 full Hessian matrices (3136 entries) and their bounds, and 142 manuscript values; numerical checks complement the universal proofs.
abstract_tex: For a regular tournament on $d$ vertices with skew adjacency matrix $S$, the Hessian determinant $H$ that Wormald attached to its random blow-ups equals $d\det(d^2I+S^2)/\det(d^2I-S^2)$. Hence $H\neq0$ and $d/H$ is the square of a rational number, as Wormald conjectured. For the cyclic tournament it gives $\sqrt{d/H}=\bigl((d+1)^d+(d-1)^d\bigr)/\bigl((d+i)^d+(d-i)^d\bigr)$, so the associated constants tend to $\cosh 1/\cos 1=2.8559578925\ldots$; this proves a second conjecture of Wormald and identifies his numerical constant.
